{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The 2011 DSA national convention resolves that DSA’s number one political priority over the next two years be to deepen popular struggles against the neoliberal politics of “fiscal austerity”.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"A two-party consensus manifested itself in the reactionary “budget compromise” of the summer of 2011.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Congressional Super Committee will likely prioritize slashing vital social programs over cutting the military budget and restoring progressive income and corporate taxation to the pre-Reagan era.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"To counter this neo-liberal consensus, DSA will prioritize participating in social movements and protest activity that demand jobs for all and the expansion of public funding of basic human needs through the restoration of progressive income and corporate taxation.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"DSA will prioritize ending the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan and cuts to unnecessary military hardware.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"DSA locals and YDS chapters, aided by educational materials and strategic guidance from the NPC and National Office, will endeavor to be “present in every struggle” that pushes for national and state policies that prioritize jobs and human needs.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"DSA places a particular priority on working within the Occupy Wall Street movement and broadening its social base by working to build coalitions between it and the labor movement, feminist organizations, progressive electoral organizations, and community groups active in the inner city and other communities of color.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
